about.text: Manapōuri is New Zealand's largest hydro station, built in a cavern about 200 m below Lake Manapōuri's West Arm in Fiordland National Park. About 1,800 workers took eight years to build it: the first power came in September 1969 and all seven units were running by 1972. The water leaves through tailrace tunnels to Deep Cove in Doubtful Sound, and a second tunnel, finished in 2002, let the station reach its full rating, though its consent limits output to 800 MW. Plans in the 1960s to raise the lake by up to 30 m met wide public opposition, a landmark in New Zealand's environmental history.

facts.label: Commissioned
facts.note: construction began in 1964; first power in September 1969, fully operational in 1972

facts.label: Units
facts.note: in a cavern about 200 m below the lake; resource consent limits output to 800 MW

facts.label: River or lake
facts.note: Lakes Te Anau and Manapōuri supply the water; two tailrace tunnels take it 10 km to Deep Cove in Doubtful Sound

facts.label: Owner
facts.note: Meridian Energy Limited; the 1999 split directions call it Hydro Energy Limited

facts.label: Previous owners
facts.value: New Zealand Government, to 1987; Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ), 1987–99
facts.note: ECNZ took over the Crown's generation on 1 April 1987; the split directions of March 1999 moved Manapouri to the South Island SOE, Hydro Energy Limited (now Meridian Energy), from 1 April 1999

facts.label: Other ratings
facts.value: 850 MW (Meridian's maximum continuous rating with the second tailrace; consent limits output to 800 MW)
